issues.t: Automatic transmission shifts poorly or fails
issues.sym: Harsh or late shifts, the car lugging or feeling stuck in a gear, slipping, or the transmission going into limp mode on older, high-mileage cars.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic used in the Cabrio wears internally with age and is sensitive to low fluid. Problems often start once the fluid level drops, and it needs Volkswagen-spec fluid.
issues.next: Have the fluid level checked by a shop that knows this transmission, since it has no regular dipstick. Fix any leaks early; once it slips badly, a rebuilt or used unit is usually needed.

issues.t: Manual transmission grinds or fails in reverse
issues.sym: Grinding or crunching when shifting into reverse, or reverse gear that won't engage at all.
issues.why: Reverse gear problems are a common weak spot in the Cabrio's 5-speed manual as parts inside the gearbox wear.
issues.next: Come to a full stop and wait a second before shifting into reverse. If it keeps grinding or won't engage, have the gearbox and clutch checked before it gets worse.

issues.t: Power window falls into the door or stops working
issues.sym: A window rolls partway up then drops, freezes halfway, or stays stuck up or down.
issues.why: The window regulator and motor wear out, and corrosion in the window parts makes failures come back.
issues.next: Have the regulator and motor inspected together. Tape the glass up or cover the opening if it drops so rain can't get in.

issues.t: Rough idle, stalling and check engine light from throttle body
issues.sym: The engine idles rough, RPMs hunt up and down, it stalls at stops, or it hesitates when you accelerate. The check engine light may come on and automatic shifts can feel off.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body on the 2.0L engine gets dirty or fails, so the engine computer can't control idle properly.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Cleaning the throttle body and doing a basic setting with a scan tool fixes some cars; others need a new throttle body. Check for vacuum leaks too.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from plastic fittings and hoses
issues.sym: A sweet coolant smell, drips under the front of the engine, the coolant level dropping, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Plastic coolant flanges and pipes on the 2.0L engine crack and seep with age, and old hoses leak. These leaks are sometimes mistaken for a head gasket problem.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested before agreeing to a head gasket job. A cracked plastic fitting is a much simpler fix.

issues.sym: Oil or coolant seeping around the oil filter, a dropping oil level, or a low oil pressure warning.
issues.why: The O-ring between the oil cooler and the engine's oil filter housing hardens and leaks with age.
issues.next: Check the oil level and look around the filter housing. Replacing the O-ring is simple; don't run the engine low on oil.

issues.t: Water leaks into the cabin and onto the fuse box
issues.sym: Wet carpets, especially on the driver's side or behind the rear seat, damp seats, or electrical problems after rain.
issues.why: Door and top seals shrink or kink, and the soft-top drains clog, letting water in. In some cars water reached the fuse box and relays, melting the fuse box and causing a no-start.
issues.next: Clear the top drains and check the door and side-window seals. If you see water near the fuse panel, get it dried and inspected right away because it can be a fire risk.

issues.sym: The power convertible top won't go up or down, moves slowly, or stops partway.
issues.why: On cars with a power top, the hydraulic pump and its parts can fail with age.
issues.next: Check the fuse and look for hydraulic fluid leaks. A shop that knows convertibles can test the pump; you can usually close the top by hand in the meantime.

issues.t: ABS module failure and ABS light
issues.sym: The ABS warning light stays on, or the ABS kicks in when it shouldn't, such as on dry pavement at low speed.
issues.why: The ABS control module and pump fail on some cars. When the ABS is off, normal braking still works but the wheels can lock in a hard stop.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Rebuilding the control module is often an option instead of buying a new one.

issues.sym: Doors won't lock or unlock with the key or interior buttons, or the alarm goes off on its own or stops the car from starting.
issues.why: The Cabrio's central locking runs on a vacuum pump that wears out, and the factory alarm can malfunction and affect other electrical systems.
issues.next: Have the locking pump and alarm module checked. A faulty alarm can be repaired or properly disabled by a shop.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burn out and connectors melt
issues.sym: Headlights burn out often, flicker or one side goes dark. The bulb connector may look brown or melted.
issues.why: The headlight wiring connectors overheat and loosen, which shortens bulb life.
issues.next: Replace a melted connector along with the bulb; just changing the bulb will lead to repeat failures.

issues.t: Water pump leak and timing belt wear
issues.sym: Coolant drips from the front of the engine, a whining or rattling noise, or overheating.
issues.why: The water pump is driven by the timing belt and wears out with age. A failed pump or old belt can strand you.
issues.next: Replace the timing belt and water pump together at the recommended interval or sooner if you don't know the history.

issues.sym: Grease on the inside of the wheels, and later a clicking noise when turning.
issues.why: The rubber boots on the front axles crack and tear with age, letting grease out and dirt in.
issues.next: Replace a torn boot early. If the joint already clicks, the whole axle usually needs replacing.

issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed.
issues.why: Wheel bearings wear out on high-mileage cars.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked. Don't put this off, since a badly worn bearing can overheat.

issues.t: Check engine light from catalytic converter or sensors
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the car fails an emissions test, or it feels down on power.
issues.why: Aging catalytic converters and oxygen sensors are common causes of a check engine light on older Cabrios.
issues.next: Have the codes read and test the oxygen sensors before replacing the catalytic converter.

issues.sym: The battery light comes on, lights dim, or the battery keeps going flat.
issues.why: The alternator wears out on high-mileage cars.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before buying a new battery.

issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, or the compressor cycles on and off a lot.
issues.why: Older systems slowly lose refrigerant through hoses and seals.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested before recharging.

issues.t: Fuel filler neck can be damaged by a failed tire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning; after a tire failure you may smell fuel or see a leak near the fuel filler.
issues.why: If a rear tire comes apart, the tread can hit and damage the fuel filler neck, which could leak fuel and cause a fire. Volkswagen recalled these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have it done for free.

issues.sym: No symptom; the child seat anchor points may not be marked as required.
issues.why: Volkswagen recalled these cars because the child seat anchorages were not marked or described as federal rules require.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and follow the owner's manual when installing a child seat.
issues.sevReason: Missing anchor labels; not a hardware failure.
